content: 49,XXXXX syndrome, also known as pentasomy X or 49,XXXXX, is a genetic condition characterized by the presence of three additional X chromosomes. The diagnosis is confirmed through karyotyping. To date, approximately 25 cases of this extremely rare condition have been documented in medical literature worldwide. The syndrome was first described in 1963. Physical Traits Individuals with 49,XXXXX syndrome often exhibit microcephaly, which refers to an abnormally small head, and micrognathia, a condition where the jaw is undersized. Their facial features are typically rounded, and the ears are generally low-set and malformed. The eyes are upslanting and may display palpebral fissures, hypertelorism (increased distance between the eyes), and strabismus (misalignment of the eyes). The nose often has a broad and depressed nasal bridge, accompanied by epicanthal folds. The mouth may present with a cleft palate, a highly arched palate, dental abnormalities, and thick, furrowed, and everted lips. The neck is often webbed, resembling the characteristic feature seen in Turner syndrome. The hands and feet are usually small and may exhibit overlapping toes, camptodactyly (permanently bent fingers), clinodactyly (curved fingers), talipes equinovarus (clubfoot), and metatarsus varus (inward turning of the forefoot). Scoliosis, or abnormal curvature of the spine, is commonly observed, and hypotonia, or reduced muscle tone, affects the musculature. Internal Organs Cardiac abnormalities are frequently associated with this syndrome, including patent ductus arteriosus (a persistent opening between the aorta and pulmonary artery), atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, and aortic dextroposition (displacement of the aorta). The lungs may exhibit abnormal lobulation, and neonatal asphyxia is a potential complication. The ovaries are often abnormally shaped, and the uterus is typically small. Kidney hypoplasia, or underdevelopment of the kidneys, is also a noted feature. Growth and Development 49,XXXXX syndrome is associated with delays in mental, physical, and motor development. Puberty may be delayed in some cases. Behavioral and functional performance can be affected, with opisthotonoid posture (severe backward arching of the body) being a notable characteristic. A general guideline suggests that for each additional X chromosome, there is an approximate decrease of 10 to 15 IQ points.
